angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 830,666 km at 57.41 pc = 0.19 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 17.4177 +/- 0.0178 mas (same row, RUWE 1.01): 57.41 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.194 +/- 0.017 solar radii from Sozzetti et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 5278 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...648A..75S/abstract): 830,666 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.126 +/- 0.036 solar masses from Sozzetti et al. 2021, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 5278 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...648A..75S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6203 +/- 64 K from Sozzetti et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 5278 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...648A..75S/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Sozzetti et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 5278 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...648A..75S/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-5278.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.336, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
